chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both)
regarding the orchard wherein happen to be fruits such that if they were sold they would constitute wealth — is there zakat obligated upon it? He said: No.

key_terms.الثمار: Fruits, produce of trees (as distinct from grain crops)
key_terms.صدقة: Here refers to zakat (obligatory alms-tax), not voluntary charity
key_terms.مالاً: Wealth, property of monetary value — the threshold concept for zakat eligibility

ai.seo_question: Is zakat (charity) obligatory on orchard fruits in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal query put to both Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them) about whether zakat is obligated on fruits grown in an orchard that, if sold, would amount to substantial wealth. The Imam's answer is an unambiguous 'No', establishing that orchard produce (other than the four staple crops — wheat, barley, dates, and raisins) is not subject to zakat. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that zakat on agricultural produce is restricted to these four specific items, even if other fruits have considerable monetary value.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the orchard wherein happen to be the fruits, ‘What if it were to be sold, there would be wealth, would there be charity (payable) regarding it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I asked abu Ja‘far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
about a garden which has fruits that if sold becomes wealth and if there is Zakat on it. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on it.’”
